what: Study 94, part A: the coding of the 19 receivers (receivers94.py), joined to study 90 and check 92.

searched.eu-code: Commitments 9 and 10 read whole; searched: 'AI Office will', 'AI Office shall', 'the AI Office' (all 60-odd uses), 'acknowledg', 'publish', 'respond'

receivers.sender: the provider of a model with systemic risk

quotes: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned
investigate.note: Also Art. 91(1): the Commission may request documentation and information. Neither is tied to an incident report.

quotes: Where necessary and appropriate, the Commission may request providers to:
restrict the making available on the market, withdraw or recall the model.
order.note: A request that binds: failing to comply is fined under Art. 101(1)(c).

quotes: Any information or documentation obtained pursuant to this Article, including trade secrets, shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78.

The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher.
sender_failure.note: The maximum is 3 % of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher; Art. 101 applies from 2 August 2026 (Art. 113(b)).

receiver_failure.note: The Act names no consequence for the Commission or the AI Office; the Court of Justice reviews fines (Art. 101(5)), a remedy of the provider.

receivers.note: Art. 90(2): the AI Office informs the Board of measures it takes under Arts. 91-94, not of the reports it receives.

sender_failure.note: The Code names nothing; the AI Act's own duty and fine stand under EU4.

receivers.note: The Code is the signatories' commitment; the AI Office receives reports and commits to nothing in it.

receivers.sender: downstream modifiers, providers, users and other third parties

quotes: Signatories will investigate the causes and effects of serious incidents, including the information within the preceding list, with a view to informing systemic risk assessment.
not later than two days after the Signatories become aware of the involvement of their model in the incident
not later than 15 days after the Signatories become aware of the involvement of their model in the incident
pass_on.note: Two days for critical infrastructure, five for a serious cybersecurity breach, ten for a death, fifteen for other serious harm; an initial report to the AI Office, counted from the signatory's awareness.
pass_on.doubt: The duty is to report the serious incident, not to forward the third party's report as such.

receivers.note: As sender of EU4 the maker answers under Art. 101 of the Act; the Code itself names nothing.

receivers.receiver_name: the large frontier developer's internal process

quotes: including a monthly update to the person who made the disclosure regarding the status of the large frontier developer’s investigation of the disclosure and the actions taken by the large frontier developer in response to the disclosure

pass_on.note: Shared inside the company, not with a public body.
pass_on.doubt: A disclosure that reveals a critical safety incident falls under B&P § 22757.13(c)(1), fifteen days from discovery.

quotes: The court is authorized to award reasonable attorney’s fees to a plaintiff who brings a successful action for a violation of this section.
